10.1002_adma.202520776: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have achieved significantly high power conversion efficiencies (PCEs), approaching the performance of silicon‐based solar cells. However, scaling up PSCs while maintaining high‐efficiency remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a negligible efficiency loss in scalable PSCs by formate anions stabilized colloids. The formate anions enhance the charge density on colloidal surfaces, strengthening electrostatic repulsion and preventing particle aggregation. This significantly reduces colloidal size to around 30 nm and promotes homogeneous nucleation, allowing the scalable fabrication of high‐quality perovskite thin films from a small area to mini module size in ambient air. As a result, PSCs achieved PCEs of 24.30% (1 cm 2 ) and 24.10% (12.6 cm 2 , 5 cm × 5 cm mini module), with negligible efficiency loss upon scaling. To the best of our knowledge, this represents the highest efficiency reported for mini‐modules. Most importantly, the encapsulated mini module retained 95% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h of operation at maximum power point tracking in ambient air.
10.1016_j.fuproc.2026.108434: Ammonia serves as a promising hydrogen-rich carrier, with supercritical hydrothermal combustion offering a viable route for green ammonia utilization. The harsh environment in supercritical water, however, challenges material durability. This study investigates the corrosion behavior of Fe-based 316SS and Ni-based Hastelloy C276 under ammonia-containing atmospheres during the ignition/stabilization stages of hydrothermal combustion. Tests were performed at 520 °C and 25 MPa for 120 h in environments with 10,000 ppm NH 3 , 28290 ppm ethanol (when added), and oxidation coefficients from 0 to 2. Results show that 316SS suffered more severe corrosion than C276 in both oxygen-free and oxygenated ammonia-containing supercritical water. Under oxygen-free condition, insufficient O 2− and consumption of metal ions by ammonia inhibited formation of complete bilayer oxide film on 316SS. Under oxygen, thinning of the inner Cr 2 O 3 layer reduced 316SS corrosion resistance, while higher Cr, Ni content in C276 inhibited inward oxygen diffusion. However, adding ethanol altered the oxide film on 316SS to a denser outer layer and thicker inner layer with flaky, interpenetrating morphology and porous three-dimensional network structure. Conversely, ethanol caused coarse, poor protective oxide layers on C276, accelerating corrosion. These findings can provide theoretical guidance for material selection in ammonia-fueled supercritical hydrothermal combustion systems. • Corrosion behaviors of 316SS and C276 in SCW with NH 3 and C 2 H 5 OH are studied. • 316SS suffered severe corrosion than C276 in ammonia-containing SCW. • High Cr/Ni in C276 hinders oxygen inward diffusion enhancing corrosion resistance. • Ethanol densifies 316SS oxide structure but induces spallation at high O 2 . • Ethanol coarsens C276 oxides accelerating corrosion despite Cr/Mo layer formation.
10.1021_acsami.5c19551: Rechargeable aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs) represent promising candidates for sustainable energy storage; yet, their development is fundamentally hindered by irreversible zinc anode degradation stemming from corrosion and sluggish Zn 2+ deposition kinetics. Herein, to address these challenges, we pioneer zinc hexafluorosilicate hexahydrate (ZnSiF 6 ·6H 2 O, ZSF) as a low-cost, multifunctional electrolyte additive through ion coordination chemistry and interfacial engineering. Comprehensive analyses reveal that ZSF simultaneously reconstructs hydrogen-bond networks to suppress free-water activity and forms a gradient ZnF 2 /SiO 2 -rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). This SEI architecture inhibits parasitic reactions while accelerating [Zn(H 2 O) 6 ] 2+ desolvation kinetics, reduces nucleation barriers by 46.0%, and enhances Zn 2+ migration by 115.6%. Consequently, the synergistic effects enable symmetric cells to achieve exceptional cycling stability exceeding 2500 h at 4 mA cm –2 /4 mAh cm –2, a 23-fold enhancement over baseline electrolytes. Paired with α-MnO 2 cathodes, full cells retain 73.4% capacity after 2000 cycles at 2 A g –1, significantly outperforming control cells (25.1% retention). This work establishes an atomic-level electrolyte engineering paradigm through functional inorganic additives, paving the way for grid-scale deployable AZIBs.
